Use case: precise-object-edit. Illustrated Kazi IAIJUTSU / 居合斬 animation.
IMAGE 1 is the USER-PREFERRED SLASHING PROPORTIONS: authoritative head-to-torso/leg ratios, lean body, long legs, face and exact illustrated style. IMAGE 2 is the original Blue CG attack for viewing direction, real body motion and violet energy language. IMAGE 3 supplies this view's face/clothing orientation only. IMAGE 4 preserves the LONG SLIM CURVED BLADE design. Match image 1's anatomy throughout; do not use squat big-headed running proportions.
Output EXACTLY 11 frames in a uniform 4 column x 3 row grid (last cell empty), portrait canvas aspect 8:9. Face north west/back-left in every cell. Same character, no redesign. One original right-handed sword, dark narrow curved blade, same length/gold hilt. Same charcoal coat, white collar, gold waist buttons, boots, marked face and swept dark hair.
The user-corrected move is a DRAW-CUT TO THE RIGHT FROM THE LEFT HIP, then a RIGHT-TO-LEFT PULLBACK CUT. It is NOT an overhead or downward chop. Real hand/blade/hip/shoulder animation, not a stationary arm under changing effects.
Frame 0 READY: upright, sword at ANATOMICAL LEFT HIP, not whichever side is nearest the camera: in the front view his left hip is on image RIGHT, in the back view on image LEFT. In profiles the far hip may be occluded; do not switch the sword to his other hip to make it visible. The RIGHT hand reaches across his waist onto the hilt at the LEFT hip, with the LEFT hand steadying the weapon there. The existing slim curved weapon lies low along that left waist, oriented rearward like the dark horizontal weapon in the original Blue CG run. No separate sword held in front, no second weapon.
Frame 1 HIP WIND-UP: right hand grips the hilt at his left hip, shoulders and hips coil slightly left; a broad readable draw preparation, blade still at the hip. No large effects.
Frame 2 DRAW PREPARATION: begin to free the same blade from the left waist; right arm starts across the body. Tiny violet sparks only.
Frame 3 IAI DRAW START: right hand carries the blade rapidly out from the LEFT hip in a wide horizontal sweeping cut toward the right/target. A thin violet trail follows its actual path.
Frame 4 MIDDLE OF RIGHTWARD CUT: hips uncoil, sword arm/blade clearly moving right across the target lane, wide horizontal violet crescent. Turn this cut consistently with this facing, preserving anatomical handedness.
Frame 5 RIGHTWARD FOLLOW-THROUGH: complete the draw-cut to the right, hand and blade extended; first crescent moves away.
Frame 6 PULLBACK START: bend elbow and rotate hips back, bringing the blade from the right side BACK ACROSS toward the LEFT. The blade stays around waist/chest height, never lifted overhead for a chop.
Frame 7 RIGHT-TO-LEFT RETURN SLASH: a second clear sweeping cut, sword and hand travelling right-to-left across the body toward the left hip. Opposite-direction violet trail, not a downwards strike.
Frame 8 RETURN CUT FINISH: hand/blade finish back toward the LEFT waist; sharp purple-white impact EXPLOSION opens at the end of the second cut, ahead at the target.
Frame 9 FINAL EXPLOSION: the original-style sharp violet/white blast blooms, while Kazi completes the return toward his left hip.
Frame 10 RECOVERY: explosion dissipates into shards/sparks; regain the left-hip draw-ready pose. Cell 11 EMPTY.
Anatomical left/right and weapon hand stay consistent in ALL views, including rear angles. The side-right preview's first cut visibly travels toward the target on the right and the return pulls back left. No downward slash, overhead chop, thrust-only motion, early huge crescent in ready frames, early explosion, hand switching, floating blade, ghost weapons or static arm in every frame.
Keep the exact proportions of image 1 and one uniform physical scale throughout. Frame 0 is neutral standing height; bends/turns remain natural without shrinking or stretching anatomy. One common foot baseline/hip origin per cell; same body scale across all rows. Full body, blade and effects must fit INSIDE each cell with at least 20 clear transparent pixels at EVERY boundary. Uniformly fit all art to leave safe margins; never clip limbs/blade/explosion or overlap neighboring cells. Sharp illustrated detail, true transparent alpha zero, no floor/shadows/haze/background, labels, text, numbers, grid lines or watermark.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Correct Kazi's RUN ANATOMY and LEFT-HIP DRAW-READY WEAPON CARRY.
IMAGE 1 is the USER-PREFERRED SLASHING anatomy/style reference. Copy its lean head-to-torso and head-to-leg proportions exactly: same skull/head size relative to the longer torso/legs, not the squat big-headed old run. IMAGE 2 is the ORIGINAL BLUE CG RUN showing the actual low hip weapon pose. IMAGE 3 is the old run GRID edit target; its stretched horizontal posture and squat proportions are explicitly REJECTED. IMAGE 4 preserves the approved face/outfit and LONG THIN CURVED BLADE design.
Exactly 18 DISTINCT frames in a 6 column x 3 row uniform grid, landscape canvas aspect 4:3. Face north west/back-left; exact same Kazi/style/proportions in every frame and direction. Stern marked face, swept black hair, charcoal split coat, white collar, gold waist buttons, black trousers/boots, restrained purple sparks.
CRITICAL: for the ENTIRE run the sword stays at his ANATOMICAL LEFT HIP, not whichever side is nearest the camera: in the front view his left hip is on image RIGHT, in the back view on image LEFT. In profiles the far hip may be occluded; do not switch the sword to his other hip to make it visible. The RIGHT hand reaches across his waist onto the hilt at the LEFT hip, with the LEFT hand steadying the weapon there. The existing slim curved weapon lies low along that left waist, oriented rearward like the dark horizontal weapon in the original Blue CG run. No separate sword held in front, no second weapon. His hands remain in this draw-ready position while the legs run. The hilt is anchored to the left waist, not raised to his chest and not carried as a naked sword pointing forward. Follow original Blue CG low hip placement in image 2. Foreshorten or occlude correctly for this view; never swap hips/weapon hand. Keep the original long slim curved sword itself, no extra belt equipment or new weapon.
Use image 1's taller lean body anatomy and a near-upright compact run: only 5-8 degrees torso lean, normal limb lengths, compact tucked elbows/hands at LEFT waist, no horizontal body stretch or long lunges. Head/hair silhouette must remain the same as the preferred anatomy rather than fanning into an oversized aerodynamic shape. Keep coat/hair follow-through short and restrained, about half the old trailing distance. Leg reach is compact: heel/toe no farther than about 15% of standing body height ahead/behind hips.
Frame 0 left heel plants slightly ahead; 1 passes beneath hip; 2 moves behind; 3 toe-off. Frames 4-8 tuck/recover the left boot into the next forward step. Frame 9 right heel plants; 10 under hip; 11 behind; 12 toe-off; frames 13-17 tuck/recover to next frame 0. Contact feet move backward steadily on one baseline; only recovering feet lift. Preserve subtle opposite hip/shoulder movement without moving the sword off his LEFT hip. Same compact gait foreshortened in front/back views.
Head/hip height stays steady with tiny bob below 1.5% body height. No hopping, inflated heads, shortened bodies, stretchy limbs, giant coat tails or flat-still feet under the torso. Exactly the anatomy/height proportions of the preferred slashing image 1; do not squash/scale a body sideways to fake compactness.
Every frame/row has ONE shared physical body scale and foot baseline, matching all other angles. Keep the entire body, left-hip sword and all sparks at least 20 transparent pixels clear of EVERY cell edge. Fit art uniformly inside cells, no clipping or neighbor overlap. True transparent alpha zero background, no ground shadow, haze, floor, grid, text, labels, extra frames or watermark. Sharp approved illustrated detail.
